knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Waterlogging after rain calls for checking the sensor, reducing frequency and allowing drainage, after checking restriction rules. Longer run times worsen waterlogging.
Midday watering loses water to evaporation. The technician explains the trade-off, advises an earlier or later start where rules allow, and records the advice.
A sensor that stops the programme is checked and the fault recorded. Bypassing the sensor defeats the water-saving control.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied zone map with three zones, the learner sets a run time for each zone from the supplied target depth and precipitation rate, showing the calculation, within the assessor's set time.
On a supplied controller or training model, the learner sets a seasonal adjustment and labels the basis for the setting.
The learner explains to the assessor, in role-play, why a requested midday schedule is not recommended and what alternative they would offer, without bypassing any sensor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Signed calculation sheet for the three mock zones.
Controller setting record and label, signed by the assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Opening a supplied controller enclosure to alter wiring during the assessment.
Bypassing a supplied rain sensor to keep a programme running during the assessment.
